notes: Independent verification of the original others.json findings and investigation records, 2026-11-14. The original input is unchanged. Changes and rejections are recorded in others.rejects.md.

Each retained finding has an exact normalized match in its named text_file and a verified note. Sentence fragments were completed; complete slide bullets count as text edges. The source normalization and OCR artifacts are preserved.

Conditions belong to the result quote only. A condition stated elsewhere in the report, on another slide or in investigation metadata is not inherited by the finding. Null means not established by this quotation, not zero or Earth conditions.

OTHERS-013 was rejected because the SPICE report contradicts its own ethylene/propane order. OTHERS-014 is retained only as the historical report of an estimated anomaly; OTHERS-015 reports that the preliminary retest did not observe it.
OTHERS-004 records the abstract's fifty-two smoke points, not a reconciled total; the same report closing remarks say 55. Neither count is silently substituted for the other.

PSI-60 and PSI-62 findings describe objectives, hypotheses or analysis methods; they are not new flight results. PSI-115 findings identify numerical simulation separately from its literature background. PSI-117 slide results remain model or analysis.

STDCE-1 is Fluid Physics and the solder study is Materials Science. Neither contributes a combustion experiment here. SSCE is a separate experiment whose report is archived under PSI-108, not evidence that STDCE burned paper.
earth_instinct and decision_hint are interpretation, not NASA text. Hints are restricted to the quoted observation and cannot certify safety or prescribe an untested crew procedure.

Fresh NTRS title/abstract verification passed for the original four NTRS findings. Fresh NASA PDFs for the SPICE fact sheet, SLICE fact sheet and NTRS 20140017780 matched the local PDFs byte for byte. Other quotations were checked against their named cached texts; live PSI redownload and visual validation of scanned SSCE numerical values are not verified.

investigations.hardware: SPICE hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), with two added burner tube sizes and a Nikon D300s digital SLR camera

measurements: simulated particle size distributions
simulated particle number densities

findings.topic: three mechanisms behind the size difference
findings.claim: The PSI-115 final report names three mechanisms that differentiate microgravity and Earth-gravity smoke: different recirculation geometries, particle settling that removes large particles on Earth, and buoyant convection carrying condensable species toward cool surfaces.
findings.quote: Results exhibit three primary mechanisms that differentiate the microgravity and Earth gravity smoke: (1) different re- circulation geometries and volumes modify the time-temperature-concentration history of the aerosol in regions of high temperature and high vapor mass fraction; (2) particle settling eliminates large particles from Earth gravity smoke, which reduces the maximum particle size and modifies aerosol development by changing coagulation and condensation rates of the remaining particles; (3) buoyant convection can transport condensible species toward relatively cool surfaces, increasing vapor-to-particle conversion. Each of these factors tend to increase the size of particles in microgravity relative to Earth gravity. How- ever, each of these factors is also highly material- and geometry-dependent: (1) the wake dynamic becomes unimportant if nucleation occurs far downstream of the wake, or if there is a time dependent flow without a stable recirculation region; (2) particle settling is irrelevant if the condensing species forms particles that are too small to settle (the DBP considered in this work forms large particles); (3) if smoke is produced in an open environment, there may not be cool surfaces nearby to increase nucleation rates. In these situations, microgravity and Earth gravity smoke are hypothesized to be more similar.
